parameters.query: select id as tenant_id, name as tenant_name, industry as tenant_industry from tenants where slug = $1 and status = 'active';

nodes.name: Set Tenant Session (RLS)
nodes.notes: IMPORTANT: must run on the SAME connection/session as every subsequent Postgres node below, or app.current_tenant won't persist. In n8n this means these Postgres nodes must share one credential AND n8n must be configured so the Postgres node reuses a session per execution, not a fresh pooled connection per node. Verify this against current n8n Postgres node docs — connection pooling behavior has changed between versions and may require 'Execute Query' in a single node with multiple statements instead of separate nodes.

parameters.query: select system_prompt_override, autonomy_rules, escalation_thresholds from ai_config where tenant_id = $1;

insert into conversations (id, tenant_id, channel, status) select $1::uuid, $2::uuid, 'chat_widget', 'open' where $1::uuid is null or not exists (select 1 from conversations where id = $1::uuid) returning id;

nodes.name: Get or Create Conversation
nodes.notes: If conversation_id was passed and exists, this insert is a no-op (WHERE guards it) — a follow-up query (not shown, add if needed) should fetch the existing row's id in that case. Simplify by always creating a new conversation client-side per session in Phase 2 and only wire up true multi-turn resumption in a later pass.

parameters.query: select role, content from messages where conversation_id = $1 order by created_at asc limit 20;
insert into messages (tenant_id, conversation_id, role, content) values ($1, $2, 'user', $3);

nodes.name: Call Claude (turn 1)
nodes.notes: Header auth credential must send 'x-api-key: <key>' — Claude API does not use Bearer auth. Verify current header name/format against docs.claude.com before first run, since this is exactly the kind of detail that silently breaks.

parameters.query: insert into tool_call_log (tenant_id, conversation_id, tool_name, tool_input, decision) values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5) returning id;

nodes.name: Execute: Knowledge Retrieval Sub-Workflow
nodes.notes: References workflow 09 - Knowledge Retrieval by ID. Replace PLACEHOLDER_KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL_WORKFLOW_ID with the real workflow ID once that workflow is built and imported (Phase 3). This node is a forward reference — it will not resolve until then.

parameters.query: insert into messages (tenant_id, conversation_id, role, content) values ($1, $2, 'assistant', $3);
